title: Extremal mappings of tori, Teichmüller potentials and symmetric-space distance
summary: The symmetric space $X_n={\rm SL}(n,\Rb)/{\rm SO}(n)$ can be interpreted as the Teichmüller space of marked, unit volume, flat $n$-dimensional tori. It comes with a unique (up to scale) ${\rm SL}(n,\Rb)$-invariant metric $d_{X_n}$. In 1939 Teichmüller gave a modular interpretation of $d_{X_2}$ (the hyperbolic metric) in terms of an extremal mapping problem for quasiconformal dilatation. Such a modular interpretation for $d_{X_n}$ for $n\geq 3$ has remained unaddressed: the natural candidates - minimal quasiconformal dilatation, Lipschitz constant, or total energy - do not work.
